title: MODIS and VIIRS burning activity
lead: Use comparable observations to establish a historical baseline. Follow the branches for prevention, incident review, and forecasts.

nodes.label: Regional burning calendar
nodes.detail: Help users examine regional burning history and apply it to prevention, incident review, and forecasts.

nodes.label: Comparable sensor records
nodes.detail: Different footprint sizes and observation schedules can change detection counts. Test how well older MODIS and newer VIIRS records line up.

nodes.label: Historical activity patterns
nodes.detail: Explain what is typical for a place and season, and identify periods with unusually high observed activity.

nodes.label: User decisions
nodes.detail: Use consistent evidence to help firefighters review incidents and help land managers assess where preventive work may be warranted.

nodes.label: Event context
nodes.detail: Assess which independent records can explain a detection or corroborate where and when an event occurred.

nodes.label: Common activity measure
nodes.detail: Which spatial and time units make hotspot activity reasonably comparable across sensors?

nodes.label: Overlap period validation
nodes.detail: How closely do sensors agree in withheld regions or seasons, and how much do observation gaps affect the result?

nodes.label: Seasonal reference periods
nodes.detail: How can users compare recent activity with earlier years for the same season and region?

nodes.label: Unusual activity periods
nodes.detail: Which methods highlight anomalies and recurring critical windows without confusing missing observations with low activity?

nodes.label: Audience workflows
nodes.detail: Which questions should each audience answer using the calendar, map, and downloadable outputs?

nodes.label: Review priorities
nodes.detail: Which evidence supports a decision to review an observation and how can uncertainty be communicated?

nodes.label: Planned burn records
nodes.detail: Where are reliable planned or completed burn records available, and how closely can they match a hotspot in place and time?

nodes.label: Airborne observations
nodes.detail: Where can the team obtain aircraft-derived infrared perimeters, and how well can they check satellite timing and extent?

nodes.label: Prevention planning
nodes.detail: Identify candidate zones for fuel treatment based on treatment suitability and expected reduction in harm.

nodes.label: Incident review
nodes.detail: Help responders review recent detections quickly and let scientists inspect the supporting observations.

nodes.label: Future activity forecasts
nodes.detail: Estimate where and when activity is more likely and test predictions on years withheld from training.

nodes.label: Treatment suitability
nodes.detail: Which fuel, terrain, ecological, exposure, and treatment history datasets can support expert review?

nodes.label: Forecast target
nodes.detail: Estimate satellite-observed burning activity during the following seven days. Grid size and reference platform remain open.

nodes.label: Forecast validation
nodes.detail: Can retrospective forecasts using only information available at the time beat the seasonal historical baseline?

nodes.label: Detection recency
nodes.detail: What source, observation time, confidence, and corroboration should responders and scientists see?

nodes.label: Landsat imagery
nodes.detail: Check active-fire points and optical surface change where clear scenes are available.

nodes.label: Vegetation and fuels
nodes.detail: Check how mapped fuels support prevention and whether recent vegetation observations improve forecasts.

nodes.label: Smoke plumes
nodes.detail: Check plume context for recent events and whether smoke available at issue time adds forecast skill.
